root_idea.summary: The root centers on intense boiling or seething, with related extensions to agitation, gushing forth, and immediate onset.
root_idea.development: From the boiling of liquid or fire, the root extends to anger and other states of agitation, abundant effusion, and the initial surge of an action or event.

senses.definition: To boil, seethe, or surge up violently.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of a cooking pot or oven and of fire; in the Quranic passages, the boiling or seething may appear as overflowing or gushing forth.

senses.definition: Immediately; in the first surge or opening phase of an action, without delay.
senses.usage_conditions: In مِنْ فَوْرِهِمْ, it denotes coming in the first rush or at the commencement of a procedure, before settling or ceasing from motion; it can also mean at once.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of liquor, to ferment.
Of blood or wine, to flush or mantle in the cheeks or head.
Of the soul or stomach, to heave or become agitated with a tendency to vomit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Equivalent in this usage to ثَارَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of anger, to boil, become roused or excited, or make someone angry.
Of a sinew, to become swollen or distended.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation of the phrase is used especially of a horse or similar animal; the source records a variant reading alongside the anger-related interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a vein, to become agitated and flow forth with blood.
Visible inflations or knots in a horse’s vein, a varicose condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The condition is described as disapproved.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water, to well or spring forth from the earth or a source.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The emphasis is on water appearing and pouring forth from a spring or source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of assembled people, to bustle or be in a state of commotion in marketplaces.
Of the scent of musk, to spread.
To equip a balance with its two iron supports between which the tongue is set.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical expression concerning the parts of a balance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prepare the fenugreek mixture called فِيرَة for a woman after childbirth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is used with reference to the postpartum woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something boil or seethe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Causative Form IV usage as recorded in the source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The muscles of a man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the saying أَبْرِزْ نَارَكَ وَإِنْ هَزَلْتَ فَارَكَ, putting forth one’s fire while making one’s muscles lean means giving food despite injuring one’s own body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The burning heat and boiling of Hell; intense or vehement heat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use describing heat or boiling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The remaining redness in the western horizon after sunset.
Gazelles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is reported as having no singular in one usage; a singular form is disputed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The odor of musk.
The bag or receptacle of musk, including its follicle or vesicle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same expression is used for either the scent or its receptacle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sweet exhalation from camels’ skins when they are moist after returning from water.
An ebullition of anger, rage, or passion.
Freshness or newness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of taking or receiving something in its fresh or new state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first part or beginning of a period of time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the beginning of the day and of the time immediately following nightfall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place where people congregate and bustle in a marketplace.
The higher or highest part of a mountain, including an elevated hard or level area.
A particular flatus or swelling in the pastern of a horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical or veterinary term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rounded mass or collection of red sand, or sand mixed with pebbles.
Fenugreek mixed as a medicinal preparation for a woman after childbirth.
One of the two iron pieces between which the tongue of a balance is set.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is فِيَارَانِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The froth or foam that boils over from a cooking pot, or the foam mantling the surface of wine.
Boiling intensely or gushing forth abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of boiling and of water or similar substances welling or pouring forth in abundance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A blow that makes a wide wound from which blood flows abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional description of a smiting whose wound is wide and gushing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sharp or energetic, said of a man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Equivalent to حَدِيدٌ in this epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A source or spring of water; also a wave or a basin or pool.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source records variant attributions and applications of the term to these water-related objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An object that does not move or turn around.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A variant lexical distinction contrasts this use with a related term for something that moves or revolves; the explanation is attributed differently in the transmitted authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An aperture in the haunch or pelvis leading toward the interior of the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical term; the plural refers to two such apertures or pelvic parts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Two appendages of the stomach of a ruminant, each containing a small nodular lump of flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The parts are described as inedible nodular structures within the stomach region.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Swollen in the sinews, said of a horse or another beast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial adjective describing distended or swollen sinews.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Both reported lexical interpretations are retained.

cautions: Lane's printed reference to “Kur iii. 121” is historical citation notation and is not converted into a modern verse location; the example for مِنْ فَوْرِهِمْ uses the independently supplied QAC location 3:125.
Several related entries, especially فَوَّارَةٌ and فُوَّارَةٌ, preserve variant vocalizations and competing classical explanations.
